newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Multinational landing force reaches Albanian port.
newsitem.headline: Multinational landing force reaches Albanian port.

text.p: The main seaborne landing force of a multinational security mission for Albania began arriving in the western port city of Durres on Tuesday, witnesses said.

A boat carrying French troops reached Durres shortly after dawn to launch the U.N.-approved mission to protect humanitarian aid convoys in Albania. Nearly 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish troops were expected to reach Albania through Durres and Tirana airport on Tuesday.

The French transport ship Orage docked at Durres at 0700 (0500 GMT), about 15 minutes after Italian military aircraft carrying Italian paratroopers landed at Tirana airport some 40 km (25 miles) to the east.
A total of 1,200 Italian, French and Spanish troops are expected to arrive on Tuesday. An advance unit of about 100 Italian troops arrived in Albania on Friday.
Over the next three weeks the total force will grow to about 6,000 soldiers. Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Romania, Greece, Austria and Denmark are contributing troops.

The eight-nation force has been tasked to protect the distribution of aid to the troubled Balkan state, which sank into near anarchy after fraudulent savings schemes collapsed early this year. Nearly 300 people have been killed in the violence.
